messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Canary deployment 'runtime-service v2.3.4' (canary pool us-west1-canary) observes p99 latency jump ~2.8x and increased error-rate (500s) starting at ~05:12 UTC. Paging current on-call: Maya.
Maya: on it, heading to logs now. can someone paste the deploy id?
deploy-bot: Canary deploy id: deploy-2026-03-14-0512 (initiated by CI pipeline). Targets: 6 canary pods.
Maya: quick check — tracing shows kernel fallback to legacy int8 path on canary hosts, spikes in kv-cache evictions, and long queue times on the batcher.
Sam: I see continuous-batcher push to batch_size=64 in the new runtime config diff. That seems risky for low-latency paths.
Jordan: Confirming -- host-uw1-canary-03 logs: "kernel: unsupported int8 opcode, falling back to generic kernel" repeated. Fallbacks are about 3-4x slower.
Maya: OK, two immediate mitigations: 1) flip the runtime canary feature flag to stop routing new traffic to canary, 2) roll back the canary deployment if flip isn't fast enough.
Emily: How fast can we flip flag? feature service is healthy. Command below:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/flags/runtime_canary -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"enabled":false}'
```
Maya: Doing flag flip now.
Maya: (reacted with :white_check_mark:) Flag toggled to false. Confirming routing delta: traffic to canary pools down to 0.5% -> 0. Backpressure should reduce immediately.
Linus: Nice. Meanwhile I recommend we reduce batch_size default in the config to 16 and restart canary pods if they remain. That will help head-of-line queueing.
Sam: I can prepare a config patch. But if the kernel fallback is due to a missing compiled kernel for the quantized op, warming or rolling back is better.
Jordan: Agree. The new optimizer in v2.3.4 added a kernel selection heuristic that misdiagnosed some int8 patterns on Ampere instances.
Maya: Decision: short-term: flag flip (done) + scale down canary to 0 pods (deploy rollback scheduled). Medium-term: rollback canary image. Long-term: revert heuristic and add regression test.
Emily: I kicked off rollback: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/runtime-service --to-revision=20260313-1200` (deploy tool queued). deploy-bot: rollback started; monitoring will report status.
deploy-bot: Rollback completed on canary pool at 05:22 UTC. Canary pod count is 0.
Linus: After rollback, p99 on us-west1 normalized to baseline within ~4 minutes. Error-rate dropped back to normal.
Maya: On-call handoff: I'm staying to monitor for 30m to be safe, then hand to Linus at 06:00 UTC. Linus, you'll take the overnight watch.
Linus: Ack, I'll take over. Initial checks: run `kubectl logs -l app=runtime-service -n prod --since=10m | grep 'falling back'` and verify zero occurrences.
Sam: For immediate postmortem data collection, I'm saving metrics: p50/p95/p99, QPS, batch queue depth, kernel-fallback counts, and affected customer list.
Maya: Customer impact: observed latency and 500s for a small percentage of requests for customers routed to us-west1 canary. Noted accounts: AcmeApp (internal id: acct-482), FinTech-Alpha (acct-193). Reached out to account execs, no SLA breach expected but FYI.
Jordan: Any sign of retries causing cascading errors in downstream services? Traces show some client retries, but gateway error-rate spike was localized and short-lived. No broader cascade.
Emily: Created INC-2026-1187 and linked logs/graphs in the ticket. Please add notes if you run extra sweeps.
Maya: Post-mitigation steps: 1) create a canary gating test for kernel-availability per instance type, 2) add a runtime regression test that simulates batching under realistic traffic, 3) revert the optimizer heuristic in the next patch.
Sam: I'll open PRs: one to revert heuristic, one to add a large batch integration test, one to add a preflight kernel check in the deploy pipeline.
Linus: Also recommend we implement a hard kill-switch in the routing plane that can immediately cut traffic to a canary pool without relying on external flag service (single RPC inside control-plane).
Maya: Good suggestion. Add to postmortem.
Jordan: Quick note: if anyone sees residual elevated latencies after 06:30 UTC, ping me.
Maya: Handing to Linus now for overnight. Summary: Canary deploy caused kernel fallback + oversized batching causing p99 spike. Flag flip + rollback mitigated within ~10 minutes. Customers notified, incident ticket created.
Linus: Taking over. Will keep monitoring dashboards and paging if anything unusual reappears.
Maya: Thanks team. Closing pager for now. :thumbsup:
Linus: (reacted with :eyes:) Will follow up in the postmortem doc tomorrow.
deploy-bot: Note: automatic rollback action logged under deploy-2026-03-14-0512 -> rollback-2026-03-14-0522.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1187 created and assigned to eng-runtime for postmortem.
Emily: Linking postmortem checklist and assigned owners: Sam (root cause), Maya (on-call timeline), Linus (remediations).
Maya: Ending thread — will add timeline+graphs to INC-2026-1187."
